items.informal_name: Degree of $ p - q $ is Less Than $ \deg p $ When Leading Coefficients Are Equal
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {p q : Polynomial R},
  p.degree = q.degree → p ≠ 0 → p.leadingCoeff = q.leadingCoeff → (p - q).degree < p.degree
items.informal_description: For any non-zero polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ over a ring $ R $, if $ \deg(p) = \deg(q) $ and the leading coefficients of $ p $ and $ q $ are equal, then $ \deg(p - q) < \deg(p) $.

items.informal_name: Strict Degree Reduction via Leading Term Cancellation in Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {p q : Polynomial R},
  p.natDegree ≤ q.natDegree → 0 < q.natDegree → (p.cancelLeads q).natDegree < q.natDegree
items.informal_description: If the natural degree of a polynomial $ p $ is less than or equal to that of another polynomial $ q $, and $ q $ has positive natural degree, then the natural degree of the polynomial obtained by canceling the leading terms of $ p $ and $ q $ is strictly less than the natural degree of $ q $.

items.informal_name: Degree Reduction via Leading Term Cancellation with Commuting Coefficients
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {p q : Polynomial R},
  p.leadingCoeff * q.leadingCoeff = q.leadingCoeff * p.leadingCoeff →
    p.natDegree ≤ q.natDegree → 0 < q.natDegree → (p.cancelLeads q).natDegree < q.natDegree
items.informal_description: Let $ p $ and $ q $ be polynomials over a commutative ring with commuting leading coefficients. If $ \deg(p) \leq \deg(q) $ and $ q $ is non-constant (i.e., $ \deg(q) > 0 $), then the natural degree of the polynomial obtained by canceling the leading terms of $ p $ and $ q $ is strictly less than $ \deg(q) $.

items.informal_name: Leading Coefficient of Polynomial Subtraction with Degree Inequality
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {p q : Polynomial R}, p.degree < q.degree → (p - q).leadingCoeff = -q.leadingCoeff
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ over a ring $ R $, if $ \deg(p) < \deg(q) $, then the leading coefficient of $ p - q $ is equal to $ -\text{lc}(q) $, where $ \deg $ denotes the degree and $ \text{lc} $ denotes the leading coefficient.

items.informal_name: Leading Coefficient of $ p - q $ When Degrees Are Equal and Leading Coefficients Differ
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {p q : Polynomial R},
  p.degree = q.degree → p.leadingCoeff ≠ q.leadingCoeff → (p - q).leadingCoeff = p.leadingCoeff - q.leadingCoeff
items.informal_description: For polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ over a ring $ R $, if $ \deg(p) = \deg(q) $ and their leading coefficients $ \lc(p) \neq \lc(q) $, then the leading coefficient of $ p - q $ is $ \lc(p) - \lc(q) $.
